PullRequest.Title: docs: consolidate design guidance and add draft component specs
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Design guidance is spread across instructions and skills, and some of it repeats values already defined in code. This PR gives contributors one place to start, `.github/skills/design-system/SKILL.md`, and puts component-specific advice beside the implementation.

The 38 draft specifications cover 16 foundations, 3 patterns, and 19 reusable components. For example, `radio.design.md` explains when arrow keys move selection, while the design-token instructions point to the registrations that define current values and replacements.

The specifications are optional guidance, not a requirement for every new control. They can be read as Markdown without a viewer. The refactor changes contributor and Copilot guidance, not product UI, token values, styles, animations, or build configuration.

### Rendered documentation

[Browse the rendered docs](https://chryw.github.io/vscode-design-system/snapshots/snapshot-v0.6.0/). These browser views show the same docs in the separate, optional Explorer; its UI is not part of this PR.

**Typography:** foundation guidance pairs design decisions with source-backed specimens.

![Typography foundation guidance and a type specimen in the Explorer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/88c46b55-f8e4-489d-828e-7ab50663f68f)

**Button:** usage guidance sits beside a real product example. Accessibility guidance and API declarations follow below.

![Button component guidance and a real VS Code Button example in the Explorer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/971c10fc-b6c1-4660-b7b6-8ca8659c5e95)

### How to verify

- `node .github/skills/design-system/scripts/validate.mts --list` — listed all 38 specifications.
- `node .github/skills/design-system/scripts/validate.mts` — validated their metadata, placement, and source bindings.
- `node --test .github/skills/design-system/scripts/validate.test.mts` — all 6 tests passed.
- `pnpm run oxlint .github/skills/design-system/scripts/validate.mts .github/skills/design-system/scripts/validate.test.mts` — passed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run VS Code and interact with the documented controls, overlays, themes, and motion.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing product startup, input, layout, and rendering paths are unchanged. The diff adds Markdown beside implementations but changes no product implementation, stylesheet, registration, or build configuration.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: User interactions and visible controls do not acquire any new per-event or per-control executable work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing product scheduling is unchanged; no new tasks or concurrent effects are started by these documents.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No product cache changes. Optional presentation metadata has no demonstrated new executable consumer in the product.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete 61-file inventory and all diff pages: executable additions are only the standalone validator and its tests. Searches in src and build found no executable references to the new discovery symbols or design-document paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: External viewer implementations are not included in the PR and cannot be used to infer new rendering cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: richer documentation and source bindings alone do not establish changed product work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Find design guidance during an ordinary UI contribution.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Contributors can read the relevant Markdown directly. The skill routes to existing local specifications and shared guidance; running discovery is optional, and ordinary UI work does not require documentation validation.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Relevant documents selected for a task, not an obligatory traversal or rendering of all 38 specifications.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No scripted fan-out is required for ordinary guidance lookup.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new code-level document cache or mandatory reread loop is introduced. Editor or assistant document-loading behavior is outside the changed implementation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the bounded routing contract in the added SKILL.md and changed entry-point instructions. No executable product or build path starts the optional validator.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The host assistant's implementation and document-loading policy are not supplied, so additional context-processing latency cannot be quantified or attributed concretely.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: reorganized guidance does not prove eager loading of all documents or mandatory extra subprocesses.

Scenarios.Scenario: Explicitly list design specifications with validate.mts --list.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: main awaits discoverDesignSpecs, then projects and serializes the inventory. Directory discovery, bounded front-matter reads, and configured source-path validation must finish before the CLI prints the list; all work is outside product startup and interaction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the checkout and recursively enumerate three specification roots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One root realpath and three recursive readdir API calls per listing; recursive work scales with directories and entries under the roots, not merely the 38 matching files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This standalone discovery command did not exist; ordinary UI workflows had no such traversal and still do not require it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The explicit listing waits for traversal before it can return.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open each matching specification and read UTF-8 chunks until its YAML front matter closes, then close the handle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: 38 opens and closes for the current inventory, typically one 4096-byte read each; the front-matter limit bounds reads to roughly 68 KiB per invalid or maximum-sized document.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No standalone specification inventory existed; the PR introduces bounded metadata reading only for explicit discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Metadata is required for the resulting inventory. Bodies are not fully loaded.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve configured source paths and stat them to verify existing files inside the checkout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Approximately 33 reference occurrences in current metadata, each issuing a realpath and a stat on success. Duplicate references are rechecked; fixtures, API member names, and ordinary Markdown links do not trigger file reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These checks did not exist before the new opt-in tooling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Configured binding checks finish before listing completes; source contents and TypeScript declarations are not loaded.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Project the discovered metadata into a JSON inventory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One JSON serialization of 38 compact inventory entries; specimens and full Markdown bodies are excluded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no equivalent new inventory output before this command.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Three discovery roots, including src/vs; traversal scales with their directory entries. The current inventory has 38 specifications and approximately 33 source-reference occurrences, including repeated references to the same implementation or CSS file.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Roots and specification reads are awaited serially. Array-valued example metadata uses Promise.all, while object properties and reference checks are serial within their owners. Current metadata produces only a small local burst, not per-repository subprocess or network fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No persistent or in-flight cache. Each invocation rescans; warm operating-system filesystem caches can reduce I/O latency. Source references are checked per occurrence, not deduplicated, but remain a small configured collection in this PR.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in call count, serialization, bounded reads, disposal, and await ordering from the complete validator diff and metadata. The filesystem work is intentional standalone discovery, not a newly hot product path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Directory count, storage latency, and measured CLI duration are not supplied. No realistic evidence establishes pathological cost at this inventory size.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: expected linear discovery and a small collection of source checks are bounded and explicitly invoked; no high-confidence unnecessary scaling mechanism is established.

Scenarios.Scenario: Validate changed specification metadata, placement, and source bindings.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: validateDesignSystem awaits checkDesignPlacement and the same discovery described above, then obtains one Git identity and prints a small report. Only this explicit documentation command waits; no changed build or product workflow invokes it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the root, traverse the specification roots, read bounded metadata, and validate configured source paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One discovery pass per validation, three root realpath calls along the wrapper chain, three recursive readdir calls, 38 bounded metadata reads, and approximately 33 realpath/stat reference pairs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No such standalone validator existed. No unchanged build or product invocation has been moved onto it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The explicit validation report waits for these checks; product startup, rendering, and ordinary UI contributions do not.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one subprocess after successful discovery, regardless of specification count; --list launches none.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The documentation validator and identity query are new, but existing product and build scenarios did not perform them and still do not.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks this CLI's final report, not a user-interface or shared service event loop.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize the checkout root, single commit identity, and validation status.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs only when reporting the explicit command's result.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The same three roots, 38 specifications, and approximately 33 reference occurrences as listing, followed by one Git query independent of collection size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Discovery follows the serial and small metadata-array concurrency above. The Git subprocess runs synchronously after filesystem validation and has a 180-second timeout; no subprocess burst occurs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The invocation has no reusable discovery cache and benefits only from operating-system caches. There is no retry loop or negative-cache mechanism. It performs discovery once, not once per specification after collection validation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the direct call path, subprocess arguments, and searches of package scripts, build, and GitHub workflows, which revealed no automatic integration.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Git and filesystem duration were not measured; a synchronous subprocess in a single-purpose CLI alone does not establish a performance bug.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the synchronous boundary is a single explicit CLI query, not collection fan-out or UI blocking. No concrete removed performance regression warrants blame provenance.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run the standalone validator's six tests.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The explicit Node test runner awaits test fixture setup, discovery assertions, and finally cleanup. One test lists a tiny temporary checkout through a child Node process; the final test scans the real checkout once.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: .github/skills/design-system/scripts/validate.test.mts: createCheckout, writeSpec, tests and finally blocks
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create temporary fixture directories and files, invoke bounded discovery, and recursively remove fixtures in finally.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Five temporary checkouts across the fixture-based tests with bounded case tables; one full-checkout discovery in the Colors test.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These new standalone tests did not exist and are not wired into existing product startup or build configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only explicit test completion waits for fixture I/O and discovery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke Node once with validate.mts --root <temporary checkout> --list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One child Node process on a five-specification fixture; no Git subprocess is used by listing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No previous corresponding test process existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The explicit test waits synchronously for CLI output.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Six tests; most create five specifications in a small temporary tree. Invalid-metadata cases repeat discovery of that small fixture, not a full checkout scan per case. Only the Colors test uses the full product tree.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No test opts into concurrent cases; each table-driven case awaits its writes and discovery before the next. One synchronous child invocation verifies CLI output on the small fixture.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Fixture discovery is deliberately repeated to test distinct mutations and root normalization. No long-lived cache or retained temporary checkout is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete test diff: temporary fixtures are cleaned in finally, repeated negative cases use small inputs, and the subprocess does not scan the full repository.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Test duration is not measured. No new automatic test integration or resource amplification is shown.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: bounded test-only work and reliable cleanup do not create a realistic product performance issue.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all 61 changed files and every diff page against base 67e393d367352baa41996239dc0dec2627df691c. Reviewed standalone discovery and validation, metadata serialization, source-check cardinality, effective concurrency, bounded reads, cleanup, caller integration, and ordinary UI/runtime scenarios. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance findings and no concrete performance regression fix were established. Static review only; external viewer implementation is outside this PR.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
